out.other_title: Definition of the two-agent debate game (answers, alternating statements, judge)
out.rationale: The authors contrast their results with what they describe as a stricter protocol proposed by Irving et al., in which only a sub-component has to be judged to validate the entire debate, and report that judging over full debate transcripts is already useful for producing expert labels using only non-experts and untrustworthy experts. Irving et al.'s simplest debate game, the record targeted here, already has the judge see the whole debate (q, a, s); the authors study such full-transcript judging empirically, with findings that generalise to different base LLMs as debaters and judges and to human judges, which fits EXTENDS.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Debate protocol design: the authors' full-transcript judging relative to Irving et al.'s simplest debate game, in which the judge sees the whole debate (q, a, s), not the stricter sub-component protocol the authors also attribute to Irving et al.; holds for LLM debaters with LLM or human judges
